column14: The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce. — Oracle Corporation, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended May 31, 2026 (filed 2026-06-23)
column15: Company first cut 'thousands' in March 2026 (termination email cited only 'a broader organizational change'; Oracle declined to comment on the AI link — originally coded press_inferred). Oracle's FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-06-23) then explicitly named AI as a workforce-reduction driver, UPGRADING this row's attribution to explicit_company. causal_link=mixed: the 10-K lists AI alongside management/product changes, performance, strategic shifts, and acquisitions, and analysts tie much of the reduction to pandemic-era over-hiring plus an AI-capex refocus. COUNT stays undisclosed: the audited FY26 figure is ~21,000 roles / ~13% (headcount ~162,000 -> ~141,000 over the year), $1.84B restructuring cost vs $374M prior FY — but that is a CUMULATIVE MULTI-ROUND FULL-YEAR total, not a single-event count, so it is documented here rather than entered as this row's count (avoids mis-bucketing/double-counting). The 'up to 30,000' figure is a TD Cowen analyst estimate, never company-confirmed. India >12,000 / rescinded IIT-NIT offers are press-reported, not in the 10-K quote.
